# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 66 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 66 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_066_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 4 — Why Hermas Was Given to the Angel of Punishment

**66:1** "Lord," I asked, "why have I been assigned to this angel of punishment rather than to the angel of righteousness?" "Because you have sinned greatly," he said. "You were delivered to this angel for discipline, so that he could humble you and bring you low until you learn what you need to learn."

**66:2** "But lord," I said, "I don't know what great sin I've committed." "Your sins are numerous," he said, "but not so extreme that you had to be permanently assigned to this angel. The real issue is that your household committed great and terrible sins against the Lord — and for that reason, you were handed over to this angel."

**66:3** "But I didn't sin," I insisted. "I didn't sin against the Lord." "Oh yes, you did," he said. "You see, the sins of your household members are your sins too. You neglected your household. You allowed it to become completely corrupt. So you share in their sins."

**66:4** "Now that I've heard and understood all this, lord," I said, "let me ask you about something else: can people who have been put through these torments repent and be saved?" "They can repent," he said, "but they can't be saved quickly. The person who has been handed over to this angel has to go through the full extent of their torments, be brought low, and complete every day of their punishment — only then can they be saved."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the personal accountability dimension of Hermas's experience with the angel of punishment.*
